messages:
maya.dev: heads up — customer-tiered routing fallback: we had a case where eu-prod fell back from model-x-32k to model-x-8k and the tooling layer broke. need a compact compatibility matrix for tokenizer/context/tool-calling before we enable auto-fallback across tiers. :grimacing:

sam.p: ugh, that matches a bug i saw. the tool-caller expected `func_call.name` to be preserved, but small-variant renames some function params.

igor.k: quick checklist: tokenizer (bpe vs spm), context length, kv-cache layout (same key ordering?), and tool-call schema. also charset/normalization differences — emoji and ZWJ sequences caused token shifts.

nina.ops: suggestion: conservative defaults for fallbacks: allow fallback only when tokenizer parity==exact OR when tool-calling is disabled for that route. otherwise return 429 or queue to same-variant pool.

ali.s: +1. also need telemetry flags so we can see when fallback actually changed output shape. i propose events: `fallback.attempt`, `fallback.allowed`, `fallback.denied`, `fallback.mismatch_reason`.

ops-bot: deploy check: canary group=platform_autofallback_v2 scheduled at 2026-03-21T09:00Z — status: pending.

leo.research: throwing an example matrix here. i know it's ugly but will help decisions:

```
Compatibility Matrix (rows = capability, cols = fallback result):
- tokenizer: exact | best-effort | incompatible
- context: same | truncated-ok | shorter-than-required
- tool_calling: full-parity | rename-only | missing-attrs
- kv-cache: compatible | rekey-required | incompatible

Rules:
- allow fallback if tokenizer==exact AND (context in {same,truncated-ok}) AND tool_calling != missing-attrs
- deny fallback if tokenizer==incompatible OR context==shorter-than-required OR tool_calling==missing-attrs
```

maya.dev: nice. for console UX we need a per-route warning badge that indicates "fallback-risk: high" (red) vs "fallback-safe" (green). also a link to the exact mismatch reason so support can triage quickly.

sam.p: implementation detail: we should calculate a compatibility score server-side (0.0-1.0) and surface thresholds in the console + webhook. score = weighted(tokenizer_score, context_score, tool_call_score, kv_score). default threshold 0.8 to allow auto-fallback.

igor.k: tokenizer_score idea: 1.0 if identical tokenizer model id + vocab checksum, 0.7 if same tokenization algorithm and vocabulary overlap >90%, 0 otherwise. need a small utility to compute overlap quickly from vocab fingerprints.

ali.s: telemetry event schema suggestion (straight string names): ["fallback.attempt","fallback.result","fallback.reason_code","fallback.tokenizer_checksum","fallback.vocab_overlap_pct","route_id","customer_tier","region","request_id"]

nina.ops: quotas note: if fallback to cheaper variant is allowed, quota accounting must be per-original-route, not per-variant, otherwise customers see weird billing. we need a flag `billing_invariant=true` on policy.

maya.dev: action items: 1) finalize compatibility matrix doc 2) add server-side score + reason codes 3) console UX: badge + drilldown 4) telemetry + billing flag 5) canary rollout gating. who's on it?

sam.p: i'll prototype the score function and config schema. will post PR to infra-routing.

leo.research: i'll write the vocab fingerprint tool (small mapreduce job) and a quick proof-of-concept that computes overlap in ~200ms for 50k vocab.

igor.k: i'll add the reason codes and wire them into runtime fallback decisions. need a short list of canonical codes: `TOKENIZER_MISMATCH`, `TOOLCALL_INCOMPAT`, `CONTEXT_TRUNCATED`, `KV_MISMATCH`, `BILLING_BLOCKED`. share opinions.

ali.s: fine with those. add `DEPRECATED_VARIANT` for variants with known regressions.

ops-bot: canary pipeline triggered by @sam.p, job id: canary-4821. logs will be at https://ci.internal/canary-4821

nina.ops: docs/console copy: "Auto-fallback may change tokenization, context handling, or tool-call signatures. When risk is high, the route will not fallback automatically — an admin can override." keep it short.

maya.dev: one more edge: tool-calling parity when `function.return_schema` differs but `name` matches. If return fields missing, some SDKs crash. i'd prefer to treat missing return keys as incompatible.

sam.p: agreed. treat return-schema-subset as incompatible for safety. we can add a passthrough mode that returns a synthetic wrapper object, but that needs opt-in.

leo.research: note for research: small-variant quantization can change token boundaries slightly for some unicode combos — will add to matrix as tokenizer fuzziness warning.

maya.dev: thanks team. i'll draft the compatibility page and include the matrix + console mocks. expecting a PR from @sam.p and @igor.k by EOD Fri. :thumbsup:
